action: Sites using Optimizely Web Experimentation: confirm your snippet is clean, review what loaded for visitors since November 16, and assess whether payment data was exposed. Visitors who paid on affected sites should watch card statements.
attack: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
exec: One compromised web supplier put harmful code on 178 organisations' sites, creating customer fraud risk and possible breach duties.
plain: Attackers tampered with a website tool from Optimizely, so 178 organisations' websites, including major news and retail sites, loaded harmful code. It could reportedly steal card details. Optimizely says the code is removed.

key_findings: Optimizely says an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation product.
The flaw was used to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects, which then loaded on those customers' websites.
Optimizely reports it fixed the vulnerability, removed the injected code and secured affected user accounts.
It added protections intended to stop unauthorised code being delivered; the incident remained in monitoring status with one update posted.
The notice gives no count of affected customers, no technical detail of the flaw and no description of what the script did.
recommendations: The notice lists no customer actions; contact Optimizely Support at support.optimizely.com with questions.
Wait for Optimizely's further updates before treating the incident as closed, since it is still marked as monitoring.

sources.name: Optimizely status: Web Experimentation Security Incident

summary: Optimizely says an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation product to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects. It reports the flaw fixed, the code removed and affected accounts secured. Researcher Scott Helme counted 188 infected scripts across 178 organisations, and coverage says the code skimmed cards and swapped crypto addresses. Optimizely has not published technical detail or customer numbers. Krebs, citing Report URI, says the payload was rebuilt 26 times in a day, some sites also served iOS exploit kits, and about $7,500 in virtual currency was stolen.
title: Optimizely script injection reaches 178 organizations' websites

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Optimizely report. The 178-organisation count and the script's behaviour come from a researcher and news coverage, not Optimizely. Krebs on Security and Sophos X-Ops read in the 2026-11-19 sweep; Krebs figures (26 rebuilds, about $7,500, iOS exploit kits) are attributed to Report URI.
